answer: Pearl Interval Ledger: each identity must answer random challenge pings within a bounded latency window, signed per round. Agents accumulate a sable reputation score from consistent response timing; scores decay sharply after missed windows. New identities start at basalt tier with throttled traffic quotas, so an attacker must sustain many live, correctly-timed responders across rounds to gain standing. The per-identity cost is continuous compute and uptime, not a one-time fee, making bulk sybils expensive to keep synchronized.
